rawOutput.title: Personal Finance Fundamentals
rawOutput.topic: Budgeting, credit, debt, and index-fund investing
rawOutput.rationale: This mixed conceptual and problem-solving plan begins with budgeting as the foundation, then introduces interest, credit, debt repayment, and investing in prerequisite order. Practical examples and bounded tasks keep each session manageable. The final session shifts from teaching to independent application and repair.

sessions.title: Build a working budget
sessions.objective: Connect income, expenses, savings, and cash flow in a usable monthly plan.
sessions.amountLabel: One monthly budget with a cash-flow check and savings priority
contentTargets: Fixed, variable, and irregular expenses
Monthly cash flow and emergency savings
completionEvidence: Classify sample expenses as fixed, variable, or irregular
Construct a balanced monthly budget from a sample income and expense list
Explain how an emergency fund changes the budget

sessions.title: Understand interest and credit
sessions.objective: Explain how borrowing costs grow and identify the main behaviors that affect credit.
sessions.amountLabel: Two interest comparisons and one credit decision
contentTargets: Simple and compound interest in borrowing
Credit reports, scores, utilization, and payment history
completionEvidence: Compare the total cost of two borrowing examples
Explain how interest and minimum payments affect a balance
Apply credit factors to choose between two card-use scenarios

sessions.title: Create a debt repayment strategy
sessions.objective: Prioritize debts while accounting for interest costs, minimum payments, and cash-flow limits.
contentTargets: Debt avalanche and debt snowball approaches
Minimum payments, extra payments, and repayment tradeoffs
completionEvidence: Compare avalanche and snowball repayment orders
Construct a repayment order for a sample set of debts
Explain the tradeoff between interest savings and motivation

sessions.title: Learn index-fund investing basics
sessions.objective: Build a basic model of diversified, long-term investing and its risks.
sessions.amountLabel: One comparison of diversified funds, costs, and risk
contentTargets: Stocks, bonds, index funds, and diversification
Fees, risk, time horizon, and compound growth
completionEvidence: Explain how an index fund differs from an individual stock
Compare two sample funds using diversification and fees
Apply time horizon and risk considerations to a sample goal

sessions.title: Make an integrated financial plan
sessions.objective: Retrieve and apply the core principles to a realistic financial scenario.
sessions.amountLabel: One integrated budget, debt, credit, and investing case
contentTargets: Priority-setting across savings, debt, and investing
Credit and interest decisions within a complete financial plan
completionEvidence: Construct a financial plan for a sample household
Explain the order chosen for emergency savings, debt payments, and investing
Compare the plan with an alternative and repair one weak decision
